# Pantheon — Repository Setup

## OpenCode Setup

Setup: [INSTALLATION.md](docs/INSTALLATION.md).

- Requires a supported host: OpenCode 2.x (the V1 contract was removed in 2.0).
- Test: focused slice checks ONLY (`node --test tests/<slice>.test.mjs`, `pytest -k`); `npm test` is strictly prohibited during dev loops and reserved exclusively for final PR/release validation.
- Lint: `npm run lint`

## Global Installation Testing (Sandbox)

Validate global installation AS A REAL USER in the sandbox `~/pantheon-sandbox/` (outside the repo; with dedicated HOME, npm prefix, and venv); the dev environment is NOT suitable for packaging tests.

- Run: `bash ~/pantheon-sandbox/run-test.sh` (MCPs, doctor, TUI)
- Agent rule: validate global installation (npm pack, `init`, MCPs, hooks) in the sandbox — NEVER in the development environment
- Teardown: `rm -rf ~/pantheon-sandbox`

## Worktrees

- Never create worktrees inside the main project; use `<project-parent>/.pantheon-worktrees/<repo-basename>/<task>`.
- Worktrees do not live inside `.pantheon/`.

## Conventions

- TDD: RED→GREEN→REFACTOR for testable behavior; use focused checks for micro-edits (sub-10s test slices)
- Never run unconstrained test suites (`npm test`) during implementation loops; full suites are for CI/release gates only
- Stronger gates (auth, security, data-integrity, coverage) are canonical in the global `Test Economy` section
- Async/await on all I/O
- Type hints on all functions
- PRs always update the README: document new features, behaviors, env vars, and commands before opening.
